blocks.content: The primary objective of TRAI is to provide a fair and transparent policy environment which promotes a level playing field and facilitates fair competition.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: TRAI was established to create and nurture conditions for the growth of telecommunications in India.
A core objective is to provide a fair and transparent policy environment that promotes a level playing field and facilitates fair competition.
TRAI is responsible for fixing and regulating tariffs for telecommunication services in India.
Protecting consumer interests and ensuring high Quality of Service (QoS) are primary regulatory mandates of TRAI.
The adjudicatory and dispute settlement functions were separated from TRAI and transferred to TDSAT through the 2000 amendment.

rows: Regulatory, tariff formulation, and advisory body
Adjudicatory tribunal for dispute resolution and appeals
Sets standards, regulates tariffs, and protects consumer interests
Adjudicates disputes between licensor, licensee, service providers, and consumers

items: TRAI is a statutory body established under the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997.
Remember that TDSAT was created in 2000 to divest TRAI of its adjudicatory powers, separating regulatory functions from dispute resolution.
TRAI's regulatory scope includes both Telecommunications and Broadcasting/Cable services.
